title: Tsiolkovsky in touch with angelic beings
summary: Jesse Michels tells of Tsiolkovsky in touch with angelic beings, about an unknown time at Russia, and relays what a named person told them. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: chowski believed that he was actually in touch with Angelic beings and he talks about and writes about it
Chikovski in Russia was the same way. He believed he had this worldview called cosmism where he thought he was in touch with angelic beings
tellings.difference: Names his worldview as cosmism and is told by the host directly, without crediting Pasulka.
tellings.link_reason: Both tellings say Tsiolkovsky in Russia believed he was in touch with angelic beings.

as_told.title: Tsiolkovsky's cosmism and contact with angelic beings

tellings.quote: Constantine chikovsky believed in nhi and that he was you know he believed in this and he wrote books about it and he's the father of Russian rocketry
tellings.difference: Told by Pasulka herself as a belief in NHI, and adds that he was the father of Russian rocketry.
tellings.link_reason: Both say Tsiolkovsky, the father of Russian rocketry, believed in non-human or angelic beings and wrote about them.

tellings.quote: the Russian space program was inspired by early rocket scientists like Constantine seosi who had basically constructed his own Cosmic religion or worldview around space
tellings.difference: Frames it as a cosmic religion that inspired the Russian space program, without mentioning angels.
tellings.link_reason: Tsiolkovsky's self-built cosmic worldview is the cosmism-and-angelic-contact story already held.

tellings.quote: josi believed that he was actually in touch with Angelic beings and he talks about it and writes about it
tellings.link_reason: Same claim that Tsiolkovsky believed he was in touch with angelic beings and wrote about it.

tellings.quote: As Diana Pasulka points out in American Cosmic, Tsiolkovsky believed that non-human intelligences, what he called ethereal beings, were communicating with us through celestial symbols.
tellings.difference: Calls them 'ethereal beings' communicating through celestial symbols and cites American Cosmic.
tellings.link_reason: Tsiolkovsky's belief that he was in contact with non-human, angelic or ethereal beings, credited to Pasulka.

plain: Konstantin Tsiolkovsky was a Russian thinker often called the father of Russian rocketry, and podcast host Jesse Michels says he believed he was in touch with angelic beings and wrote about it, at first crediting the religion scholar Diana Pasulka. Michels later links it to Tsiolkovsky's worldview called cosmism, while Pasulka herself describes it as his belief in non-human intelligence, which he wrote books about. It matters to them because it suggests the space age had roots in contact with other beings.
